title: 考研英语（旧）2009年真题及答案解析（整卷）

sentences.text: Habits are a funny thing.
sentences.translation: 习惯是一种有趣的东西。我们不假思索地依赖习惯,让大脑进入自动驾驶模式,放松地沉浸在熟悉惯例带来的无意识舒适中。19世纪William Wordsworth说过:"支配不加思考的群体的不是选择,而是习惯。"在瞬息万变的21世纪,即使"习惯"这个词本身也带有负面含义。

sentences.text: We reach for them mindlessly, setting our brains on auto-pilot and relaxing into the unconscious comfort of familiar routine.
"Not choice, but habit rules the unreflecting herd," William Wordsworth said in the 19th century.
In the ever-changing 21st century, even the word "habit" carries a negative implication.
So it seems paradoxical to talk about habits in the same context as creativity and innovation.
sentences.translation: 因此,在创造力和创新的语境下谈论习惯似乎自相矛盾。但大脑研究人员发现,当我们有意识地培养新习惯时,我们创造了平行路径,甚至创造了全新的脑细胞,这些可以让我们的思维列车跳上新的、创新的轨道。

sentences.text: But brain researchers have discovered that when we consciously develop new habits, we create parallel paths, and even entirely new brain cells, that can jump our trains of thought onto new, innovative tracks.
But don't bother trying to kill off old habits; once those ruts of procedure are worn into the brain, they're there to stay.
sentences.translation: 但不要费力去消除旧习惯;一旦那些程序化的惯性轨迹在大脑中形成,它们就会一直存在。相反,我们刻意植入自身的新习惯会创造出可以绕过那些旧路径的平行通道。

sentences.text: Instead, the new habits we deliberately press into ourselves create parallel pathways that can bypass those old roads.
Most tests require collecting cells by swabbing saliva in the mouth and sending it to the company for testing.
sentences.translation: 大多数检测需要通过在口腔中擦拭唾液来采集细胞，并将其送到公司进行检测。所有检测都需要一个潜在的候选人来进行DNA比对。

sentences.text: All tests require a potential candidate with whom to compare DNA.
Critics also argue that commercial genetic testing is only as good as the reference collections to which a sample is compared.
sentences.translation: 批评者还认为，商业基因检测的质量取决于用于比对样本的参考数据库的质量。一些公司使用的数据库并不依赖于系统收集的数据，而是将来自不同研究项目的信息混杂在一起。这意味着DNA数据库可能有来自某些地区的大量数据而缺少其他地区的数据，因此一个人的检测结果可能因处理结果的公司不同而有所差异。此外，公司用于估计关系的计算机程序可能已获得专利，不接受同行评审或外部评估。

sentences.text: Databases used by some companies don't rely on data collected systematically but rather lump together information from different research projects.
This means that a DNA database may have a lot of data from some regions and not others, so a person's test results may differ depending on the company that processes the results.
In addition, the computer programs a company uses to estimate relationships may be patented and not subject to peer review or outside evaluation.
The relationship between formal education and economic growth in poor countries is widely misunderstood by economists and politicians alike.
sentences.translation: 经济学家和政治家都普遍误解了贫穷国家正规教育与经济增长之间的关系。这两个领域的进步对于这些国家以及所有其他社会的社会、政治和智力发展无疑都是必要的;然而,教育应当成为促进贫穷国家经济快速发展的最优先事项之一这一传统观点是错误的。我们很幸运事实如此,因为在那里建立新的教育体系并让足够多的人接受教育以改善经济表现需要两到三代人的时间。一家研究机构的研究结果一直表明,所有国家的工人都可以通过在职培训实现生产率的大幅提高,从而实现生活水平的大幅提高。

sentences.text: Progress in both areas is undoubtedly necessary for the social, political, and intellectual development of these and all other societies; however, the conventional view that education should be one of the very highest priorities for promoting rapid economic development in poor countries is wrong.
We are fortunate that it is, because building new educational systems there and putting enough people through them to improve economic performance would require two or three generations.

The findings of a research institution have consistently shown that workers in all countries can be trained on the job to achieve radically higher productivity and, as a result, radically higher standards of living.
Ironically, the first evidence for this idea appeared in the United States.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2009/section2-part-a-3/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好Honda, Nissan, and Toyota achieved about 95 percent of the productivity of their Japanese counterparts –a result of the training that U.S. workers received on the job.具有讽刺意味的是,这一观点的第一个证据出现在美国。不久前,当美国进入经济衰退而日本处于泡沫前的巅峰时期时,美国劳动力被嘲笑为教育水平低下,并被认为是美国经济表现不佳的主要原因之一。日本过去是、现在仍然是全球汽车装配生产率的领导者。然而研究显示,Honda、Nissan和Toyota在美国的工厂达到了其日本同行生产率的约95%——这是美国工人接受在职培训的结果。

sentences.text: Not long ago, with the country entering a recession and Japan at its pre-bubble peak, the U.S. workforce was derided as poorly educated and one of the primary causes of the poor U.S. economic performance.
Japan was, and remains, the global leader in automotive-assembly productivity.
Yet the research revealed that the U.S. factories of

More recently, while examining housing construction, the researchers discovered that illiterate, non-English-speaking Mexican workers in Houston, Texas, consistently met best-practice labor productivity standards despite the complexity of the building industry's work.
sentences.translation: 最近,在考察住宅建设时,研究人员发现,尽管建筑行业工作的复杂性,德克萨斯州休斯顿的不识字、不会说英语的墨西哥工人始终达到了最佳实践劳动生产率标准。

sentences.text: As education improved, humanity's productivity potential increased as well.
sentences.translation: 随着教育的改善,人类的生产潜力也随之增加。当竞争环境促使我们的祖先实现这一潜力时,他们反过来又能负担得起更多的教育。这种日益提高的教育水平可能是先进经济表现所需的复杂政治体系的必要条件,但不是充分条件。因此,如果没有政治变革,贫穷国家可能无法摆脱贫困陷阱,而这种政治变革可能只有通过更广泛的正规教育才能实现。然而,缺乏正规教育并不会限制发展中国家劳动力在可预见的未来大幅提高生产率的能力。相反,提高生产率方面的限制因素解释了为什么那里的教育发展速度没有更快。

sentences.text: When the competitive environment pushed our ancestors to achieve that potential, they could in turn afford more education.
This increasingly high level of education is probably a necessary, but not a sufficient, condition for the complex political systems required by advanced economic performance.
Thus poor countries might not be able to escape their poverty traps without political changes that may be possible only with broader formal education.
A lack of formal education, however, doesn't constrain the ability of the developing world's workforce to substantially improve productivity for the foreseeable future.
On the contrary, constraints on improving productivity explain why education isn't developing more quickly there than it is.
The most thoroughly studied intellectuals in the history of the New World are the ministers and political leaders of seventeenth-century New England.
sentences.translation: 新大陆历史上研究最为透彻的知识分子群体是十七世纪新英格兰的牧师和政治领袖。根据美国哲学标准史的记载，在殖民地时期的美国,没有任何其他地方"对智力追求给予如此重视"。根据许多书籍和文章的说法,新英格兰的领袖们确立了美国知识生活中一个不断展开的、占主导地位的清教传统的基本主题和关注重点。

sentences.text: According to the standard history of American philosophy, nowhere else in colonial America was "so much importance attached to intellectual pursuits."
According to many books and articles, New England's leaders established the basic themes and preoccupations of an unfolding, dominant Puritan tradition in American intellectual life.
The early settlers of Massachusetts Bay included men of impressive education and influence in England.
sentences.translation: 马萨诸塞湾的早期定居者中包括在英格兰受过良好教育且颇具影响力的人士。除了1629年之后十年间来到马萨诸塞教会的约九十位博学的牧师外,还有像约翰·温思罗普这样的政治领袖,他在前往波士顿之前是一位受过教育的绅士、律师和王室官员。这些人著述颇丰并广泛出版,影响了新大陆和旧大陆的读者,使新英格兰充满了认真治学的氛围。

sentences.text: Besides the ninety or so learned ministers who came to Massachusetts churches in the decade after 1629, there were political leaders like John Winthrop, an educated gentleman, lawyer, and official of the Crown before he journeyed to Boston.
These men wrote and published extensively, reaching both New World and Old World audiences, and giving New England an atmosphere of intellectual earnestness.
Meanwhile, many settlers had slighter religious commitments than Dane's, as one clergyman learned in confronting folk along the coast who mocked that they had not come to the New World for religion.
sentences.translation: 与此同时,许多定居者的宗教信仰不如戴恩那样虔诚,正如一位牧师在面对沿海地区的民众时所了解到的,这些人嘲笑说他们来新大陆不是为了宗教。"我们的主要目的是捕鱼。"

sentences.text: "Our main end was to catch fish."
